notes: Phase logic matches questionnaire.json: phase 1 = regular eating (questionnaire adjustment phase 1), phase 2 = ultra-processed swaps (starts once snaq_total >= 15 and skips are 0-3/week for two check-ins). skippedMeals rules are phase 1 or any; upfItems rules are phase 2 except 'upf-add-side' (additive only, never restrictive). All thresholds are app rules, not validated cutoffs. reasonMatch uses the app's log values (no-time, no-appetite, forgot, no-food-available, other); questionnaire skip_reasons use different ids (no_time, no_appetite, forget, no_food). Left out for lack of solid evidence: reminder frequency/cadence rules, stress-specific tips (not a logged skip reason), and 'out of sight' home-food-environment claims. Frequent no-appetite skips plus weight loss trigger the doctor note in questionnaire.json (rule skip-no-appetite-doctor). Extra fields beyond the requested schema: top-level 'notes' and per-rule 'notes'. Revision 3: every rule has allergens[] (FDA major allergens + gluten, same vocabulary as foods.json; empty when the tip names no allergen foods) and, where relevant, alternativesIfAllergic {allergen: replacement text}.

rules.tip: A few meals slipped by this week, and that happens. Try choosing one meal and an if-then plan for it, like "If it's noon, then I eat lunch, even if it's small."
rules.why: If-then plans (implementation intentions) reliably help people act on intentions they already have; the effect on adding healthy eating behaviours is medium-sized.
